change_summary: PLOS ONE issued an expression of concern on this paper, which is not a retraction. It says Fig. 7 does not match its legend and text, so the LSD1 siRNA migration statement is unsupported, and that the Fig. 4 LSD1 blot may have a discontinuity and the transfection controls are insufficiently described. It also says similarities with other groups' work call the validity and provenance of the results into question, and that the authors did not respond. The paper's knockdown and overexpression findings on proliferation, migration and invasion rest on the transfection experiments the notice questions, so they are in doubt.
evaluation: Your Section 3 (Rationale for Aim 2) cites [12] for the H460 scratch-assay knockdown result and calls it the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration. The notice says the paper's Fig. 7 does not match its legend and text and contains no LSD1 siRNA experiment, so this use is touched. Your Section 2 cites [12] for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue than in normal lung tissue; it is uncertain whether this is touched, because the notice's specific issues do not name the tissue data but its provenance concern could reach all results. Overall the impact is medium: the notice is an expression of concern rather than a retraction, and it hits the result your central hypothesis leans on.
recommendation: The notice is an expression of concern, not a retraction, and the findings are in doubt but not withdrawn. Your Section 3 cites [12] for the H460 scratch-assay knockdown result and calls it the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration, and the notice says Fig. 7 does not match its legend and text and reports no LSD1 siRNA experiment. Hedge that sentence, cite the notice, look for independent support, and don't build Aim 2 on this result. Your Section 2 cites [12] for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue, and the notice questions the validity and provenance of the reported results, though it does not specifically name the tissue data. Add a light hedge there and cite the notice; tracking continues, so a retraction would raise a new alert.
